title: fix(chat): keep End at the bottom while tool results stream
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pressing End in the transcript while tool results stream can stop thousands of pixels above the bottom. The full overlapping-stream reproduction on the base leaves Chromium 7,250 px short (82,430 / 89,680).

## User Impact

Plain End on the transcript uses the same manual follow action as Latest. Nested scrollports, editable targets, modified keys, and already-cancelled input retain native handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pane already owns manual follow intent. Route admitted End to that owner and prevent the competing native default. Also renew its existing end destination when the stream grows after virtual-core's five-second scroll journey expires, without restarting prepared rows or introducing another timer/state owner.

The earlier routed-only prototype already prevented default, so the proposed uncancelled-native-animation explanation does **not** explain its historical 4,428 px miss. That exact miss did not recur in detailed, light, minimal or pre-lookup replays; its writer remains unproven. The expired-journey gap is separately reproduced by the new regression test, red on base and green here.

## Evidence

Acceptance: real keyboard End during a 400-message / 200-tool overlapping stream reaches within 8 px of the end; Latest, exact order, retained results, and native PageUp ownership remain checked. PageUp retains the strict 2 px drift bound. This is a correctness fix, not a performance claim.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chromium baseline End, full stream overlap | Fails: 7,250 px short |
| Chromium and Firefox fixed End | Pass: 0 px; Latest, order and retained tool checks pass |
| Strict native PageUp, stream released by actual keydown | Chromium and Firefox base/head pairs all fail with the same 4 px drift. Assertion remains strict; no tolerance increase. This inherited failure is not claimed fixed. |
| Offset observer + transcript owner unit tests | 45 pass; expired native destination test fails on base and passes on head |
| UI and scripts typechecks, scoped lint, format/diff checks | Pass |
| Production build + strict same-machine bytes | Pass; see table below |
| Production Knip | Same failure text on base and head: existing unused exports in daemon/launchd, gateway/config-write-flow, provider-external-auth, provider-runtime, dashboard-tools, and types in plugins/types. No new ignore. |
| Independent autoreview / simplify | No actionable P0–P2 finding; existing pane and scroll-command owners retained |

Final CI: [attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42716479663/attempts/2) retains only two inherited UI E2E shards. `session-ownership.e2e.test.ts` / `aligns Person left status at 1200 px` and `390 px` fail at line 370 (14 px gap versus 13); `native-conversation.e2e.test.ts` / `keeps a single web conversation with in-page native navigation and Dashboard handoff` fails at line 241 (56 px header versus 64). The same cases and actual/expected values fail on [the merge-base scheduled main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42711813458); native-conversation is in a different shard there. The native inherited-failure route retains these failures.

The initial attempt also failed the collapsed-question touch-expansion case (`question-footer.test-support.ts:138`, composer count 1 versus 0). That case passed on scheduled main and in focused local runs of both base and head. One diagnostic rerun of its CI shard passed; this is an unresolved intermittent failure, not a claimed product fix or inherited attribution. No test or production behavior was weakened for it.

The final matched browser run uses fresh headless processes. Full Chrome repeatedly crashed creating later contexts with CVDisplayLink errors on this logged-out host. The explicit software-rendering launcher (`--disable-gpu`) produced 62 frames in 1,016 ms; no timings from this correctness fixture are used as performance evidence. WebKit's opening and closing smoke launches both timed out; it is unavailable. A later fresh-process full-Chromium workload also passed without the software override; the follow-on census will use that original launcher.

| Surface | Base | Head | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS, normalized gzip | 91,766 B | 91,766 B | 0 B |
| Startup CSS, normalized gzip | 38,756 B / 1 request | 38,756 B / 1 request | 0 B |
| Chat JS, normalized gzip | 1,298,479 B | 1,298,084 B | −395 B |
| Chat JS, served gzip | 1,305,408 B | 1,305,473 B | +65 B |
| Chat JS requests | 20 | 20 | 0 |

Existing new-session and total-CSS budget overages do not grow; no budgets changed. Touched production LOC 2,290 → 2,322 (+32); tests 1,337 → 1,401 (+64); harness 4,093 → 4,233 (+140); docs 167 → 174. The dedicated 64-line test allocation covers End admission/default behavior and the expired-destination regression. Solid effect/render-effect/untrack/listener/query/owner API counts are unchanged (all zero); the pre-existing imperative flush remains 1 → 1.

Focused browser command: `scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts --fresh-browser --engines chromium,firefox --steps event-load-pageup,event-load-end --viewport desktop --pairs 1 --bundle-dir <head> --compare-bundle-dir <base>`. Builds and strict performance checks use the same machine. Broad UI coverage runs in PR CI with `ci:full`.

Before: native End stops above the final result.

After: the manual end destination stays owned through the stream.

![After: End reaches the final result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ceff708-c2f8-45e7-b025-3b6720633aab)
